answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust through walks capped at \(k\) steps, limiting how far influence can diffuse. A sybil cluster like a nebula behind a walnut-sized gateway has low conductance, \(\phi(S)=w(S,V\setminus S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\), so only limited trusted walk mass can enter. Min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore constrain its aggregate voting weight by external support, not claimed node count; the trellis of cross-attestations must be substantial to earn more.
